messages:
Mira K: paging: customer SRE (Jen) just reported widespread 5xxs for their private deployment after today's config push. ALB in front of their vpc is returning 502/503s, traffic spike is only to a single customer domain.
Incident Bot: Incident created - INC-1922500000 - Severity: P1 - Automated alert: >50% requests 5xx to customer-alb-prod (target group unhealthy).
Jen (customer-sre): seeing 100% error rate for endpoints under /api/v1 on their domain, can confirm it's not app-level timeouts. Downstream services in their tenant are healthy.
Sam Chen: copying net-eng + security. Mira can you paste the ALB target health and WAF logs?
Mira K: quick grab: ALB target group shows 0/3 healthy, failed health checks: TCP reset. WAF logs show repeated rule "rate-limit-global-50ps" firing from shared WAF policy. Suspect global rate-limiter applied to shared ALB config.
Taylor (ops): that WAF policy was updated in the last deploy (0800 UTC) to tighten a rule. It was intended for hosted customers but maybe the rule was attached to the wrong listener.
Rita (net-eng): pulling listener config now. If the rule got attached at listener-level it might be matching the customer's host header incorrectly.
Arnold (oncall): @Mira can you confirm whether Route53 record changed in the same deploy? Need to rule out DNS flip.
Mira K: Route53 records unchanged. DNS resolves to the expected ALB IPs. But I see a listener rule with host header `*` that has the WAF ACL attached. That seems wrong.
Leo R: owning rollback options: we can either remove the WAF ACL from that listener, or create a traffic-routing rollback to dedicated pool. Which is less risky?
Luis (sec): removing WAF ACL temporarily has security implications, but given it's causing complete outage for a single enterprise customer it's acceptable as a short mitigation if we add monitoring and limit to 10m.
Claire PM: customer impact confirmed: enterprise tenant has degraded UX for all users, high priority for CSM. Keep customer updated.
Jen (customer-sre): We need an immediate fix; can you also enable a quick fallback so traffic goes to their dedicated pool (if available)? That would minimize user impact.
Taylor (ops): quick play: 1) detach global WAF ACL from ALB listener 2) patch listener rule to match only hosted domains 3) if still flaky, flip Route53 weight to the dedicated pool. I'll run 1 now.
Taylor (ops): running: `aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:alb:... --default-actions ...` detaching WAF ACL...
Mira K: command returned success. WAF ACL detached at 1922500060.
Incident Bot: Action logged by Taylor (ops): detached WAF ACL from listener (action id a7f3).
Jen (customer-sre): error rate dropping from 100% -> 18% in the last 30s. Seeing some slow responses but no hard 5xxs.
Rita (net-eng): listener rules still have a catch-all host header. I'll patch the rule to add customer-specific host match so shared rules don't apply.
Rita (net-eng): applying rule patch: adding `Host: tenant-orion.example.com` then reorder.
Mira K: rule update applied at 1922500120. WAF ACL still detached. Health checks start returning healthy for targets, 3/3 healthy by 1922500180.
Leo R: good. let's not remove WAF ACL permanently. Option: reattach ACL to a more-specific listener or move this tenant to a separate ALB with proper isolation. Both are follow-ups.
Luis (sec): require a postmortem and change control before we reattach. Also need to confirm the new WAF rule didn't get rolled out to other shared listeners.
Taylor (ops): rolling out temporary monitoring alert to watch for false negatives: `rule: tenant-5xx > 5% for 1m` and `waf: global-rate-limit-fire` tagging.
Mira K: Customer is reporting recovery. Jen, can you confirm user experience?
Jen (customer-sre): confirmed. Traffic largely normal now. We'll keep verifying on our side for 30m. Thanks for fast turnaround.
Arnold (oncall): handing off to post-incident oncall: @Leo you'll own the follow-up RCA and remediation actions. I'll annotate the runbook and assign.
Leo R: will do. Immediate action items: (1) create isolation checklist for private deploy ALB listeners (2) audit last 7 deploys for listener-wide WAF attachments (3) propose moving enterprise tenants to dedicated ALBs or apply stricter listener host matches.
Claire PM: I'll coordinate communication with CSM and schedule a postmortem with customer tomorrow at 1500 UTC.
Luis (sec): ensure we have WAF log snippets and who approved the rate-limit change. Tagging security review.
Incident Bot: Incident INC-1922500000 closed (mitigated) at 1922500280 - Severity downgraded from P1 to P2 after partial recovery.
Mira K: quick note for the postmortem: avoid listener-level wildcard WAF attachments for multi-tenant ALBs; prefer per-tenant match rules or explicit per-ALB ACLs. Also consider a deploy-time check to prevent global ACL changes on shared listeners.
Jen (customer-sre): thanks all. appreciate the quick containment. We'll follow up if anything resurfaces. :heart:
Taylor (ops): copying commands & diffs to the incident doc. I'll open internal ticket to move this tenant to dedicated ALB and schedule a config guard.
Leo R: assigning RCA to myself, ETA for doc + fixes: 48h.
Mira K: closing thread here, will attach logs and start the RCA draft.
